_doc: Cabinet firsthalf horizon variant -- the sim counterpart of the real-robot
'higher-firsthalf' setup, which ends once the blocking object is moved aside and the
drawer is pulled open (the full-horizon real policy is 'higherZ').
Applied at load time by maniguard.eval.horizon_override to the SAME dict that datagen
reads as `diagnostics` and eval reads as `scene_info`, so the success check and the
language instruction change together in both pipelines. The bench on disk is never
LTL safety is inherited unchanged and is deliberately not listed here: cabinet's three
constraints are pure safety formulas (G ...), which stay meaningful on a truncated
min_position CALIBRATION: the drawer is pulled to `open_dist`, which the datagen
reachability search derives per task and then derates by OPEN_DIST_SAFETY=0.88, so it
is a fixed constant for this task but is not recorded in the bench. The value below is
set from the ACHIEVED end-of-demo joint positions measured over the collected demos
(see _calibration). It is a LOWER bound, not a band: the drawer has a hard stop, and a
policy that pulls it further than the demonstrations did has done better, not worse.

_calibration.note: Servo overshoot is single-sided positive (every demo ended PAST the commanded 0.2546), so the bound needs no margin for undershoot. The threshold sits below the commanded distance: a policy need only pull to where the demos were told to pull, not reproduce the overshoot. Well clear of the historical half-open failure mode (~0.127). Used by BOTH the datagen gate and eval -- one number, one meaning.

cabinet_pickup/task_0019/base.prompt: Open the cabinet drawer on the table. Do not knock over anything else.
